title: Roadmap
text: scope: dock_extension providing chat panel. Provider-neutral chat construction consuming board’s new_llm_model_option(). LLM tools CRUD operations blocks, links stacks. Block-parameter editing via blockr.core’s external-control mechanism (external_ctrl = TRUE blocks). Streamed responses tool-call telemetry via shinychat. Explicitly scope (now): Building LLM provider abstractions — ellmer handles . Persistence conversation history — deferred later phase blockr.session. Mutation safeguards (undo, dry-run, snapshot--mutation) — initial implementation applies tool calls directly board. Snapshotting likely revisited blockr.session exposes right hooks. Multi-board / multi-session reasoning — assistant context scoped single board mounted .

title: Roadmap
text: Concretely: new_assistant_extension() returns dock_extension whose UI shinychat::chat_mod_ui() panel whose server constructs ellmer::Chat board’s llm_model option, registers tool layer closures (board, update, session), hands chat shinychat::chat_mod_server(). tool R closure captures live board update references. Inspection tools read board$board. Mutation tools emit update(list(blocks = …, links = …, stacks = …)) payloads, write externally-controlled block reactives. chat’s system prompt composed fixed assistant persona plus dynamically generated board summary (block IDs, types, links, stacks, available block constructors).

title: Roadmap
text: Two decisions shape every phase deserve stated front: Provider neutrality via new_llm_model_option(). never construct ellmer chat client directly. board exposes llm_model board option whose value chat-constructor function signature function(system_prompt = NULL, params = NULL) returning ellmer::Chat. extension reads option calls . Providers, model names keys configured globally via blockr_option("chat_function", …) — scope package. option always resolves usable function (falling back blockr.core’s default_chat), extension never needs handle missing chat backend. Narrow tools, auto-batched dispatch. LLM sees many small, focused tools (add_block, add_link, …) rather one monolithic modify_board. tool call dispatch update(...) immediately; stages change pending payload held inside extension server. Validation runs current board merged pending payload, per-tool feedback meaningful. assistant’s turn completes, accumulated payload flushed single update(...) call. combination gives us: LLM-friendly tool ergonomics (small, focused calls, easy describe). single atomic dispatch per user turn (one validation pass, one re-render, one logical snapshot point future blockr.session integration). “add link block” ordering trap disappears within turn — ordering stage operations irrelevant long final payload valid. staging layer central architectural deliverable package; every mutation tool thin façade .

title: Roadmap
text: phase corresponds design-doc vignette, named p<n>-<topic>.qmd (p prefix keeps file names portable — R CMD check rejects vignette names starting digit). Phases ordered package compiles demos something end one. File: p1-shell.qmd new_assistant_extension() constructor, dock UI/server, shinychat::chat_mod_ui / chat_mod_server panel, ellmer::Chat constructed board’s llm_model option. Includes day one: Streaming responses, history, basic cost/token telemetry. visible “stop” affordance backed ellmer::stream_controller() (cheap wire, runaway tool-calling assistant without stop button later unpleasant). default, overridable assistant persona shipped package — configurable via system_prompt argument new_assistant_extension(). default persona short scoped “blockr board assistant”; subsequent phases add dynamic board context top. tools yet — assistant can hold conversation board-blind. File: p2-read-tools.qmd Establish “tool kit” abstraction: closures (board, update, session), JSON-schema argument definitions via ellmer::type_*, result shaping (strings, structured lists, errors). Implement read-inspection tools: list_blocks, describe_block list_links, list_stacks list_available_block_types get_block_result_preview phase locks patterns later mutation phases follow. File: p3-staging.qmd architectural keystone. new LLM-facing tools, clean foundation Phase 4. pending-update reactiveVal private extension server. “merge current board + pending payload” helper tools validate . turn-completion hook flushes pending payload via update(...) resets . Error formatting tool results (model can self-correct). Behaviour flush failure (partial rollback, error user, error model). File: p4-mutation-tools.qmd thin façades Phase 3 staging layer: Blocks: add_block(type, args), remove_block(id), modify_block(id, args) (via external_ctrl reactives). Links: add_link(, , input), remove_link(id). Stacks: add_stack(blocks, name), remove_stack(id), modify_stack(id, blocks, name). Design decisions nail : ID generation policy, validation constructor args staging, behaviour external control available modify_block target, link validity checks (referenced blocks exist, target input exists, cycles). File: p5-polish.qmd Dynamic board-summary system prompt (refreshed turn). Model-facing error formatting recovery hints. Example apps inst/examples/. top-level tutorial vignette blockr.assistant.qmd. README, pkgdown site setup. new features beyond polish context layer. Phase 4 turns larger expected, natural split block mutation vs. link + stack mutation. Blocks carry bulk complexity (external control, registry lookup, ID generation); links stacks mechanical block patterns place. cheap retroactively — design doc cleaves boundary.

text: flagged don’t lose , explicitly phases initial roadmap: Snapshot / undo — integrate blockr.session snapshot board state mutation expose undo tool LLM. Requires hooks blockr.session don’t yet exist. Conversation persistence — bookmarking conversation history across sessions; partially supported shinychat::chat_mod_server(bookmark_on_*). Per-block-type tool registration — allow block packages contribute tools specific blocks (e.g. blockr.dplyr block exposing set_filter_expression tool). Multi-agent / multi-tool-call orchestration — explicit support long-running plans, tool-call retries, structured planning. UI affordances tool calls — inline “approve change” UI chat, surfacing tool diffs user apply.
